title: Yamaha DSP Error on Boot
shortDescription: Receiver displays DSP ERROR and shuts down or fails to boot.
fullDescription:
RX-V and Aventage receivers run a self-test on the DSP chip at startup. If the chip fails to respond or its firmware is corrupt, the receiver shows DSP ERROR and powers off after a few seconds.

A failed firmware update is the most common cause; less often, a hardware fault on the main board.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug receiver for 10 minutes, then power on while holding STRAIGHT button.

fixSteps.title: USB recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Download recovery firmware from Yamaha, place on FAT32 USB, follow service-mode update.

whenToCallPro: If recovery firmware does not load — likely main board failure.

title: HDMI Handshake Failure
shortDescription: Receiver fails HDCP handshake with TV or source, displaying HDMI ERROR.
fullDescription:
An HDMI handshake failure occurs when one of the HDMI links cannot complete the HDCP authentication. Yamaha receivers route handshake through the DSP, so a failure on one input may break all outputs.

Usually a cable, a 4K/HDR setting, or a TV that is slow to power up.

fixSteps.title: Re-handshake
fixSteps.instruction: Power off everything. Power up TV first, then receiver, then source.

fixSteps.title: Replace cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use Premium High Speed (18Gbps) or Ultra High Speed (48Gbps) HDMI.

whenToCallPro: If receiver HDMI board failed (no input works).

title: AM Tuner Static / No Stations
shortDescription: AM band shows only static; FM and DAB work fine.
fullDescription:
Yamaha AV receivers ship with a small AM loop antenna that is easy to leave disconnected or to plug into the wrong terminals. Without a proper antenna, AM is essentially silent.

Also, AM is heavily affected by LCD TVs, LED bulbs, and switching power supplies.

fixSteps.title: Connect loop antenna
fixSteps.instruction: Snap the AM loop antenna into the AM and GND terminals on the back, follow polarity.

fixSteps.title: Reposition
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate antenna and move away from TVs, dimmers, and chargers.

whenToCallPro: Rare — only if tuner board failed.

faq.a: Some newer Aventage models drop AM in favor of DAB+ in EU markets.

title: MusicCast Network Error
shortDescription: Receiver cannot connect to MusicCast or local network services.
fullDescription:
MusicCast is Yamaha's wireless multi-room platform. NETWORK ERROR means the receiver lost connection to the MusicCast cloud, the local Wi-Fi, or a paired MusicCast device.

Usually a Wi-Fi credential issue or router blocking multicast.

fixSteps.title: Reconnect Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: Setup -> Network -> connect to Wi-Fi using the MusicCast app or remote.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Setup -> Network Update -> install latest firmware.

whenToCallPro: If Wi-Fi module failed (Bluetooth still works but Wi-Fi never appears).

faq.a: Yes, all RX-V/A receivers have an ethernet port.

title: Speaker Protection Tripped
shortDescription: Receiver enters protection mode due to speaker short or DC offset.
fullDescription:
When the receiver detects a short between speaker leads or excessive current draw, it enters protection mode and shuts off the amplifier. The display shows CHECK SP WIRES.

A stray strand from bare-wire connections is the usual culprit.
symptoms: No audio after a few seconds

fixSteps.title: Inspect wires
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect each speaker. Trim and tighten leads. Use banana plugs if possible.

fixSteps.title: Test channels
fixSteps.instruction: Reconnect one speaker at a time and run a test tone to find the faulty channel.

whenToCallPro: If protect persists with all speakers disconnected — internal amp fault.

faq.a: Yes, jumpers or extra leads can short.

title: YPAO Calibration Cannot Complete
shortDescription: YPAO room calibration aborts with No Signal or Excess Noise.
fullDescription:
YPAO uses a calibration mic plugged into the front MIC jack to measure room response. Failures occur due to background noise, a faulty mic, or low test tone level.

For RX-A models with YPAO R.S.C. and 64-bit, also check the mic stand height.

fixSteps.title: Quiet room
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off HVAC, fans, refrigerators on same wall.

fixSteps.title: Check mic
fixSteps.instruction: Use the supplied YPAO mic in the YPAO MIC jack at ear height.

faq.a: No, YPAO requires the calibrated Yamaha mic.

title: Zone 2 No Audio Output
shortDescription: Main zone works but Zone 2 outputs no audio.
fullDescription:
Zone 2 limitations on Yamaha receivers: only analog 2-channel inputs are sent to Zone 2 unless the source is also from network/USB. HDMI sources without Zone OSD are typically not routed.

Also check that Zone 2 is enabled and the speaker assign mode is set to allow Zone 2.

causes.cause: HDMI source not routable to Zone 2
Speaker assign not set to Zone 2

fixSteps.title: Speaker assign
fixSteps.instruction: Setup -> Speaker -> Power Amp Assign -> 5.1 + Zone 2.

fixSteps.title: Use analog/network source
fixSteps.instruction: Switch Zone 2 to a network source or use analog inputs.

faq.a: Yes, that is the point — main and Zone 2 can play independently.

title: Receiver Overheating Shutdown
shortDescription: Receiver shuts down after 30-60 minutes of use due to overheating.
fullDescription:
Yamaha receivers use convection cooling and rely on top/side ventilation. If placed in an enclosed cabinet without airflow, the heatsink and transformer overheat and the protection circuit shuts the unit down.

Dust accumulation on heatsinks magnifies the issue.

fixSteps.title: Provide airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Leave 4 inches above and 2 inches each side. Add a USB cabinet fan if needed.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum vents
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air at the top vents with the unit unplugged.

whenToCallPro: If overheating persists with good airflow — likely failing thermal compound on output transistors.

faq.a: Different — that is energy saving, not thermal protection.

title: IR Remote Stops Working
shortDescription: Yamaha remote no longer controls the receiver.
fullDescription:
Yamaha receivers respond to a specific IR ID. If the receiver and remote IDs drift apart, or the remote batteries die, control is lost. Some bright LED bulbs near the receiver also cause IR flooding.

Also check that ECO mode is not blocking IR wake-up.

fixSteps.title: Match Remote ID
fixSteps.instruction: Setup -> Function -> Remote Sensor -> set both ID1 or ID2 on receiver and remote.

faq.a: Yes, MusicCast app and AV Controller app work over Wi-Fi.

title: Firmware Update Failed
shortDescription: Network firmware update fails or hangs at progress bar.
fullDescription:
Network firmware updates can fail due to dropped Wi-Fi, low signal, or busy Yamaha CDN. The receiver typically reverts to the prior firmware safely on reboot.

Use the wired ethernet path or USB recovery if Wi-Fi is unreliable.

fixSteps.title: Use ethernet
fixSteps.instruction: Plug receiver into router with cat 5e/6 cable, retry update.

fixSteps.title: USB update
fixSteps.instruction: Download .bin from Yamaha to FAT32 USB stick. Hold buttons per service guide.

whenToCallPro: If receiver is bricked after update.

faq.a: Generally yes, but new HDMI standards may require it.
